**Progress M-14M** (Russian: Прогресс М-14М) was a Russian uncrewed cargo spacecraft that resupplied the **International Space Station (ISS)**. It was part of the **Progress-M** series, which is a variant of the Progress spacecraft used for logistics missions to the ISS. Below is a detailed overview of the mission:

---

### **Mission Overview**
- **Spacecraft Type:** Progress-M (11F615A60)
- **Manufacturer:** **RSC Energia** (Russia)
- **Launch Date:** **January 25, 2012, 23:06:40 UTC**
- **Launch Vehicle:** **Soyuz-U** (from **Baikonur Cosmodrome, Site 1/5**)
- **Docking Date:** **January 28, 2012, 00:09 UTC**
- **Docking Port:** **Pirs (DC-1) module** (Russian segment of the ISS)
- **Undocking Date:** **April 19, 2012, 11:04 UTC**
- **Deorbit & Reentry:** **April 28, 2012** (burned up over the Pacific Ocean)

---

### **Key Mission Details**
#### **1. Launch & Rendezvous**
- Progress M-14M was launched atop a **Soyuz-U rocket** from **Baikonur Cosmodrome** in Kazakhstan.
- It followed a **two-day rendezvous profile** (standard at the time) before docking with the ISS.
- The spacecraft carried **2.6 tons of cargo**, including:
  - **Fuel** (for ISS reboosts)
  - **Oxygen & Air** (for the station’s atmosphere)
  - **Water** (for crew consumption and experiments)
  - **Food & Supplies** (for the Expedition 30 crew)
  - **Scientific Equipment & Spare Parts**

#### **2. Docking with the ISS**
- The spacecraft docked automatically with the **Pirs module** (a Russian docking compartment and airlock).
- The **Expedition 30 crew** (commanded by **Dan Burbank**, with **Anton Shkaplerov, Anatoli Ivanishin, Oleg Kononenko, André Kuipers, and Don Pettit**) monitored the approach.
- After docking, the crew unloaded the cargo and later filled the Progress with **trash and waste** for disposal.

#### **3. Undocking & Deorbit**
- Progress M-14M undocked from the ISS on **April 19, 2012**, to make way for the next resupply mission (**Progress M-15M**).
- After undocking, it conducted **engine tests** (including a **reboost test** for future Progress missions).
- On **April 28, 2012**, the spacecraft performed a **deorbit burn** and **burned up** over the **South Pacific Ocean**, with any surviving debris safely falling into the ocean.

---

### **Technical Specifications**
| **Parameter**               | **Details** |
|-----------------------------|------------|
| **Spacecraft Mass**         | ~7,290 kg (at launch) |
| **Cargo Capacity**          | ~2,669 kg (total) |
| **Dry Cargo**               | ~1,260 kg |
| **Fuel for ISS Reboost**    | ~870 kg |
| **Oxygen & Air**            | ~50 kg |
| **Water**                   | ~420 kg |
| **Propulsion System**       | **KTDU-80** (main engine) + thrusters |
| **Power Supply**            | Solar panels (deployable) |
| **Docking System**          | **SSVP** (Russian docking mechanism) |

---

### **Significance of the Mission**
1. **Routine Resupply:** Progress M-14M was part of the **regular resupply chain** for the ISS, ensuring the crew had food, water, and equipment.
2. **Engineering Tests:** After undocking, it conducted **engine firing tests** to validate new procedures for future Progress and Soyuz missions.
3. **Preparation for Future Missions:** The mission helped pave the way for **Progress M-15M**, which introduced the **Kurs-NA** upgraded docking system.

---

### **Expedition 30 Crew (During M-14M’s Mission)**
| **Astronaut/Cosmonaut** | **Role** | **Agency** |
|-------------------------|----------|------------|
| Dan Burbank (USA)       | Commander | NASA |
| Anton Shkaplerov (RUS)  | Flight Engineer | Roscosmos |
| Anatoli Ivanishin (RUS) | Flight Engineer | Roscosmos |
| Oleg Kononenko (RUS)    | Flight Engineer | Roscosmos |
| André Kuipers (NED)     | Flight Engineer | ESA |
| Don Pettit (USA)        | Flight Engineer | NASA |

---

### **Notable Events During the Mission**
- **No Major Anomalies:** The mission proceeded **nominally** with no significant issues.
- **Post-Undocking Tests:** After leaving the ISS, Progress M-14M performed **engine burns** to test new navigation and control algorithms.
- **Reentry Over Pacific:** The spacecraft was **intentionally deorbited** to avoid space debris.

---

### **Comparison with Other Progress Missions**
| **Mission**       | **Launch Date** | **Cargo Mass** | **Docking Port** | **Notes** |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------|------------------|-----------|
| **Progress M-13M** | Oct 30, 2011   | ~2,648 kg      | Pirs             | First post-Shuttle era Progress |
| **Progress M-14M** | Jan 25, 2012   | ~2,669 kg      | Pirs             | Routine resupply |
| **Progress M-15M** | Apr 20, 2012   | ~2,700 kg      | Pirs             | First use of **Kurs-NA** docking system |

---

### **Legacy**
- Progress M-14M was one of many **successful Progress resupply missions** that kept the ISS operational.
- It demonstrated the **reliability of the Soyuz-U/Progress system**, which remains in use today (though now with **Soyuz-2.1a** rockets).
- The mission helped **test new docking procedures**, which were later used in **Progress M-15M** and subsequent flights.

---

### **Sources & Further Reading**
- **NASA ISS Mission Pages** ([NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/))
- **Roscosmos Press Releases** ([Roscosmos](https://www.roscosmos.ru/))
- **Spaceflight101** ([Progress M-14M Overview](https://spaceflight101.com/))
- **Gunter’s Space Page** ([Progress M-14M](https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/progress-m.htm))
